tools.description: Name a reviewer for a thread (G5) — the eligible set. Empty set = open review (any qualifying member). Idempotent. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: add_reviewer

tools.description: Decide a pending approval gate: accept or decline, with an optional note. Decline takes effect at once. Accept takes effect at once only for a token holding approval:grant, on a gate below the workspace's confirmation threshold (by default every gate is at or above it). Otherwise you get {status: confirmation_required, confirmation_url}: a one-time link the person opens in the Maidan console and confirms, signed in as themselves. Clients that declare URL-mode elicitation are shown the same link through elicitation. You cannot confirm for the person; do not retry, poll get_approval_gate. Nobody accepts a gate they requested. The decision records which client you used and that a model asked.

decision.description: accept or decline; cancelling stays with whoever opened the gate

note.description: optional note kept on the gate with the decision, at most 2000 characters

tools.name: approval_decide

tools.description: Assign or hand off a thread/task to a member, optionally with a handoff note delivered to subscribers on the assignment event.

assignee_id.description: member to assign the thread to

note.description: optional handoff note for the assignee

tools.name: assign_thread

tools.description: Cancel a task: close it without its work being done, park it from dispatch with the reason, and end any live claim, so the worker's next renew_claim is refused. The reason (1 to 500 characters) is posted on the thread. Requires workspace:write; without thread:transition only the member that created the thread may cancel it. Cancelling an already-cancelled thread returns the first cancel; a thread closed some other way is refused. The REST twin is POST /threads/{id}/cancel.

reason.description: why the task is cancelled, posted on the thread

tools.name: cancel_thread

tools.description: Create a thread in a channel. Requires workspace:write and access to the channel, the same rule as POST /channels/{cid}/threads. title and parent_thread_id are optional. A spawn the budget refuses is refused here too.

attributes.description: the task's attributes, stored with the thread (the shape set_thread_attributes takes, without thread_id)

acceptance.description: how a reviewer verifies the task; the worker must satisfy it

author_family.description: for a review: the provider family that wrote the change under review; claim_next never hands the thread to a claimer of that family. Once set it is kept: a later set neither clears nor changes it

lane.description: the service lane it may run in: batch (async, cheapest) or flex; omitted runs at standard rates

linear_issue.description: the Linear issue the task is for, such as ENG-123; where the workspace turned claim comments on, the claim and release are said on it

tier.description: the change's review tier; omitted reads as B in the metrics

footprint.description: the task's claim footprint, stored with the thread so the claim queue never sees it without one (the shape set_thread_footprint takes, without thread_id)

repo.description: owner/name, or a GitHub clone URL

priority.description: dispatch priority, stored with the thread; higher is claimed first (default 0)

tools.name: create_thread

tools.description: Find the thread an external reference points at: a Slack message (slack_channel and slack_ts: the thread whose result was posted as that message or into that Slack thread), a Slack channel alone (the thread it is linked to), or a GitHub pull request (repo and pr_number: the thread tracking it, linked to it, or delivering to it). Returns the thread, or null when nothing in your workspace that you may read matches. The twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/thread-lookup.

repo.description: owner/name or a GitHub clone URL; with pr_number

slack_channel.description: a Slack channel id such as C0123ABCD

slack_ts.description: a Slack message ts such as 1700000000.000100; needs slack_channel

workspace_id.description: your own workspace (whoami's workspace_id); omitted, the same

tools.name: find_thread

tools.description: Find a workspace's threads by their task attributes: equality filters over kind, engine, threat_model, size, linear_issue, tier, lane and review_family, given as attr (attr.linear_issue=ENG-123 style pairs), plus engine, tier and lane as bare shorthand, and ref (ref.twin_of=<thread id> style: relation wire name to thread id) for threads holding that reference to that thread; a thread outside your workspace matches nothing (an unused relation is an empty result too). Combined with AND. A thread with no stored attributes matches the defaults it reads with (kind=change, threat_model=false); the other fields match only a stored value. Scoped to your own workspace (workspace_id omitted, the same; a foreign one is refused) and to threads you may read. Keyset-paginated like list_threads (limit, cursor, order; a cursor that is not a thread you can read in your workspace is refused); returned threads carry their attributes. The twin of GET /workspaces/{id}/threads.

attr.description: Attribute equality filters by field name: kind, engine, threat_model, size, linear_issue, tier, lane, review_family. Values are the fields' wire forms.

cursor.description: Exclusive keyset cursor: the prior page's last thread id.

engine.description: Only threads routed to this engine (pi, session or human); shorthand for attr.engine.

lane.description: Only threads in this service lane (batch or flex); shorthand for attr.lane.

order.description: Direction of the keyset walk (default oldest).

ref.description: Reference filters by relation wire name (twin_of, duplicates, supersedes, ...): keeps the threads holding that reference to the given thread id.

tier.description: Only threads carrying this review tier (A or B); shorthand for attr.tier.

workspace_id.description: your own workspace (whoami's workspace_id); omitted, the same

tools.name: find_threads

tools.description: Poll a durable approval gate by id. Returns the gate — state is pending until a human answers, then accepted/declined/cancelled with any content they supplied — or null if no such gate exists in your workspace. Hosts with MCP Apps show it as an inline approval card.

gate_id.description: the gate id returned by request_approval

tools.name: get_approval_gate

tools.description: A member's mention inbox: recent mentions plus the read-cursor, so an agent can find what it hasn't seen. Mentions only; for everything waiting on the member (assigned tasks, requested reviews, open approval gates and unread mentions), use get_waiting_inbox.
tools.name: get_inbox

tools.description: Read a thread's review standing: required_count, approvals (distinct qualifying), and approvals_met. This is the approval side of the close-gate; a refutes edge is checked separately when closing.
tools.name: get_review_status

tools.description: Pack thread messages, edits, references, FSM history, and the workspace glossary for agent prompts. Edits are lean by default (id/editor/timestamp only); pass include_edits=true for full before/after bodies. The glossary (canonical term definitions) is included by default when non-empty; pass include_glossary=false to drop it. Pass as_of=<event_id> to replay the thread as it stood at that event-log id (deterministic over the immutable log; audit / re-ask from before a tangent). Pass token_budget=<n> to cap the message page by estimated tokens: the opening message and the recent tail are kept, the middle is folded into an auditable elision marker in fixed blocks. The result is two text parts: the stable prefix (workspace boot, brief, messages) and the volatile tail (state, lease, cursors, prefix sha256). Those strings are the bytes REST returns with split=true.

as_of.description: Event-log id: reconstruct the thread as it stood at that point (as-of replay). Omit for the live pack.

delta.description: Return a delta instead of the whole pack. The first content part is always the delta head (delta, prefix_unchanged, prefix_sha256, prefix_bytes), never empty; the second is the volatile tail. When since_prefix_sha matches the current prefix, the head has prefix_unchanged true and no messages or prefix. With message_cursor, the head adds the messages after that cursor when appending them rebuilds the prefix; otherwise it carries the replacement prefix.

include_accepted_decisions.description: Attach in-channel accepted/closed decisions (token-lean teasers) so a fresh claimer sees what the channel already decided. Waiter envelopes appear only when status is reviewed; result_kind is a namespaced string (e.g. example.review.result/1), not a closed enum. Withheld on DM channels. Set false for the leanest pack.

include_edits.description: Include full body_before/body_after on each edit (heavy); default returns edit metadata only.

include_glossary.description: Include the workspace glossary (grounding); omitted when empty. Set false for a token-tight pack.

include_parent_grounding.description: For a child thread, attach parent grounding (the parent's opening ask + latest decision) so a fresh claimer knows why the thread exists. Absent for root threads / cross-channel / DM parents. Set false for the leanest pack.

max_bytes.description: Cap the canonical pack by bytes. Elision grows by fixed message blocks until the pack fits or only the opener and newest message remain.

message_cursor.description: Page messages after this id. With delta, it is also the delta cursor.

since_prefix_sha.description: Hex sha256 of a prefix the caller already holds. Requests a delta on its own.

token_budget.description: Cap the message page by estimated tokens (chars/4): keep the opening message and the recent tail, fold the middle into an auditable 'elision' marker. Omit to cap by rows only.

tools.name: get_thread_context

tools.description: Read a task's structured result, or null if none has been produced yet.
tools.name: get_thread_result

tools.description: The thread's active agent status declaration, or null when cleared. Requires workspace:read.
tools.name: get_thread_status

tools.description: Read a thread's current steer, or null if none is set. A resuming or newly-assigned agent reads this to follow the current steering guidance.
tools.name: get_thread_steer

tools.description: The waiting-on-you inbox, everything needing a member's attention: their assigned non-terminal threads, the reviews requested from them (review_request: a thread in review naming them as a reviewer, without their approval yet), the reviews that name no reviewer and fall to them (unassigned_review: a thread in review with no named reviewer that they own, or that nobody owns when they are a workspace admin), the workspace's pending approval gates, and their unread mentions. Oldest-waiting first, each aged against sla_secs (default 86400 = 24h) with an overdue flag. One member's queue, not @everyone. For mentions alone, with a read-cursor you advance with mark_inbox_read, use get_inbox.
tools.name: get_waiting_inbox

tools.description: Pack workspace channels, thread contexts (bounded by thread_limit), and the workspace glossary (once at the top level).

include_glossary.description: Include the workspace glossary once at the top level (grounding); omitted when empty. Set false to drop it.

max_bytes.description: Byte cap applied to each nested thread pack.

token_budget.description: Cap each nested thread's message page by estimated tokens (see get_thread_context). Omit to cap by rows only.

tools.name: get_workspace_context

tools.description: List channels in a workspace.
tools.name: list_channels

tools.description: A parent thread's child threads, each collapsed to a summary with a message count — a threaded view of 'N replies' per child without loading each child's messages.
tools.name: list_child_threads

tools.description: List messages in a thread.
tools.name: list_messages

tools.description: List a member's per-recipient notifications, newest first. Set unread_only to see just the unread ones. The durable inbox the notification router fills; drain it here, then wait_for_notification for new ones.
tools.name: list_notifications

tools.description: A channel's threads ordered by last activity — most-recently-posted first. A post floats its thread to the top; a rename does not.
tools.name: list_recently_active_threads

tools.description: List per-target delivery status for a thread's structured result (disposition, external reference, last error). Empty means the result was not routed anywhere, which is valid. workspace:read + thread access.
tools.name: list_result_deliveries

tools.description: List a thread's review decisions (reviewer, decision, note).
tools.name: list_reviews

tools.description: List thread results in the caller's workspace, newest first. Optional result_kind is an exact-match facet on the namespaced string (e.g. example.review.result/1), not a closed enum. Private-channel rows the caller cannot access are omitted.

result_kind.description: exact namespaced result_kind (e.g. example.review.result/1); omit to list every accessible result

tools.name: list_thread_results

tools.description: List a channel's live threads, oldest first by default or newest first with order=newest, keyset-paginated. Default 100 (max 500); pass cursor=<last thread id of the prior page> for the next page. since (RFC 3339), result_kind and status filter in the query, before the limit.

cursor.description: Exclusive keyset cursor: the prior page's last thread id.

order.description: Direction of the keyset walk (default oldest).

result_kind.description: Only threads whose stored result carries this result_kind.

since.description: Only threads created at or after this RFC 3339 instant.

status.description: Only threads whose declared status is this one (working, needs_input, needs_review, blocked, done).

tools.name: list_threads

tools.description: Advance a member's inbox read-cursor through an instant (RFC 3339); returns the updated inbox.
tools.name: mark_inbox_read

tools.description: Mark one of a member's notifications read (recipient-scoped; marked=false if the id isn't this member's).
tools.name: mark_notification_read

tools.description: Post a message to a thread as the authenticated member.

body.description: plain text; omit when sending typed content (body is derived from it)

tools.name: post_message

tools.description: Full-text, semantic, or hybrid search over a workspace's messages. Returns ranked hits with highlighted snippets, each naming its channel (channel_name), thread (thread_title) and author (author_handle) beside their ids.

after.description: Only messages posted at/after this RFC 3339 instant (inclusive).

before.description: Only messages posted before this RFC 3339 instant (exclusive) — a half-open window with after.

embedding_model.description: Semantic/hybrid only: registered model name (default: active provider).

hybrid_weight.description: Hybrid only: semantic weight in [0,1] (default 0.5). combined = w*semantic + (1-w)*lexical over normalized scores.

snippet_only.description: Drop full message body from each hit (keep only the snippet) to save tokens.

tools.name: search_messages

tools.description: Set (upsert) a thread's dispatch priority (G3 fair dispatch). Higher = more urgent (default 0). claim_next orders by an effective rank = this priority aged up the longer the thread waits, so priority jumps the queue without starving long-waiting tasks. Requires thread:transition.
tools.name: set_priority

tools.description: Replace a thread's task attributes in full. The kind says what sort of work it is (change, plan or review), the engine says who or what it is routed to (pi, session or human), and threat_model marks work that needs a threat model. A claim_next that names an engine takes only work routed to that engine, so a Pi worker is never handed session or human work. A thread nobody described reads as a change with no engine and no threat model.

acceptance.description: how a reviewer verifies the task; the worker must satisfy it

author_family.description: for a review: the provider family that wrote the change under review; claim_next never hands the thread to a claimer of that family. Once set it is kept: a later set neither clears nor changes it

engine.description: omit to leave the work unrouted

lane.description: the service lane it may run in: batch (async, cheapest) or flex; omitted runs at standard rates

linear_issue.description: the Linear issue the task is for, such as ENG-123; where the workspace turned claim comments on, the claim and release are said on it

tier.description: the change's review tier; omitted reads as B in the metrics

tools.name: set_thread_attributes

tools.description: Set (upsert) a thread's persisted steer — durable steering guidance that survives claims and handoffs, so a resuming or newly-assigned agent reads the current steer. Latest wins.
tools.name: set_thread_steer

tools.description: Advance a thread's FSM state (start_review, close, or archive). The MCP twin of REST POST /threads/:id. Separation of duties, the required-reviewers close-gate, and unresolved refutes all apply identically — there is no MCP bypass. On a thread with a review requirement, start_review is refused until a result is posted (set_thread_result). Returns the updated thread.

action.description: start_review (open to in_review), close (in_review to closed) or archive (closed to archived). To send work back, use submit_review with request_changes

tools.name: transition_thread

tools.description: Block until the member gets a new notification-worthy event (today: mentions), or the timeout lapses. The general form of wait_for_mention. Returns the triggering event, or null on timeout. Pass since_log_id (your high-water log_id from the last drain) to also catch an event from the gap before this call subscribes; omit it for pure-live behaviour (drain with list_notifications first).

since_log_id.description: lookback anchor: replay the log for a matching event with log_id greater than this before parking live

tools.name: wait_for_notification

tools.description: Block until a task's result is produced (a thread_result_set event for thread_id), returning the result payload, or null on timeout. The coordination wait for spawn/wait/aggregate. Pass since_log_id (your high-water log_id) to also catch a result set in the gap before this call subscribes; omit it for pure-live (read get_thread_result first for an already-produced result). To put a deadline on a thread instead, use set_wait.

since_log_id.description: lookback anchor: replay the log for a matching event with log_id greater than this before parking live

tools.name: wait_for_result

tools.description: Return the authentication-bound identity: actor_id, member_id, optional delegation_grant_id, workspace_id, capabilities, capability_sets the caller fully holds, and whether the credential is a bearer. Call this first — writes are attributed to member_id.
tools.name: whoami
